text:
maria: heads up — triaging a cluster of Go vuln reports affecting our runtime and some platform services. primary libs: grpc, golang.org/x/oauth2, golang.org/x/net (http2). looks like dependency graph pulls these into the inference runtime image and a few control-plane services.

samir: can you list the CVEs and suggested pins? rough repro steps?

maria: tl;dr:
- CVE-2025-31011 (grpc): vulnerable to message framing DoS in certain streaming flows, patched in grpc v1.56.6+
- CVE-2025-29877 (golang.org/x/oauth2): token injection edge-case when parsing malformed provider responses, patch in v0.2.0+
- CVE-2025-30100 (golang.org/x/net/http2): header-parsing issue leading to request smuggling; patch in x/net v0.7.0+
links: https://security.example/CVE-2025-31011, https://security.example/CVE-2025-29877, https://security.example/CVE-2025-30100

Suggested quick pins (apply to go.mod of affected repos):
```
require (
  google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.6
  golang.org/x/oauth2 v0.2.0
  golang.org/x/net v0.7.0
)
// or run: go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.6 golang.org/x/oauth2@v0.2.0 golang.org/x/net@v0.7.0
```

maria: impact: runtime-serving (hosted API) + Dedicated control-plane, and repo: infra/image-builder references older indirect pins.

leo: noted — our dedicated runtime images are built from runtime-image:v2025-11 which uses go 1.21 and a stale go.sum. upgrading these deps will change binary hashes. we need a canary image build + perf smoke. also any ABI break? grpc patch is minor, but confirm grpc-go compatibility w/ our interceptors.

anya: triage priority suggestion:
- grpc (CVE-2025-31011) -> P0 (possible DoS under load, high CVSS)
- x/net (http2) -> P0 (request smuggling could allow bypasses)
- oauth2 -> P1 (token parsing edge-case, lower exploitability)

maria: agree. plan: create branch (security/ops/go-deps-patch), bump pins, run unit tests, then smoke canary in staging with traffic shaping (1% production traffic) for 24h, then roll to dedicated staging pools. if green, schedule a low-risk rollout with circuit-breaker and rollback window.

samir: who owns the runtime-image updates? i can take it, but need help validating interceptors. leo can you pair on smoke?

leo: yep I will pair. also we should update the Dockerfile build cache keys to force module cache refresh: add "--mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod,sharing=private" and clear go.sum before rebuild in canary.

maria: test checklist:
- unit tests + integration tests (auth flows, streaming RPCs)
- replay fuzzer for http2 headers for 6h
- verify token flows (OIDC) and metrics baseline
- confirm no increased p99 latency on streaming endpoints

dependabot: Dependabot created pull request #412: "chore(deps): bump google.golang.org/grpc, golang.org/x/net, golang.org/x/oauth2" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412

samir: nice. PR includes go.sum changes and a short description. @maria can you add the CVE refs to PR body and requested reviewers: leo, anya, samir. also mark as security patch.

maria: done — added CVE refs and a checklist. requested reviewers.

deploy-bot: build/pipeline started for runtime/pr-412 — image tag: pr-412-canary, CI: unit+integration, estimated time ~18m

anya: one more governance note: we need to record the change in the internal security tracker and trigger an audit-log export for the next compliance review. also ensure KMS keys used to sign images are present in the canary run.

maria: good call. owners + ETAs:
- samir: update runtime-image and open image build (ETA: today EOD)
- leo: perf + interceptor testing (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- anya: audit log + compliance ticket update (ETA: today)
- maria: coordinate canary rollout and PR approval (ETA: tomorrow afternoon)

samir: I'll also backport to the 1.20-build branch for on-prem customers who haven't moved (low-risk patch only) — opening backport PR after main merges.

leo: logging question — will pinning these create any new license notices? quick grep shows no new transitive MIT/BSD changes but i'll add a license check in the PR CI.

maria: final ask — if anyone sees any failing auth/stream tests during CI, ping #eng-runtime and add a short blame comment on the PR so we can revert fast. i'll post a short incident template for rollback steps. :thumbsup:

samir: ACK. starting work now.

leo: ACK. pairing tomorrow.

anya: moving compliance ticket to "in progress".

maria: thanks all — will follow up in #eng-runtime with rollout notes once canary results are in.
